title: 2012 真题 Text 3 · Gene Patents
description: 来自 2012 年英语真题 Reading Comprehension 的第三篇阅读，讨论基因专利争议及其对生物技术产业的影响。
author: 2012 English Exam
heroNote: 这篇文章法律与科技术语较多，翻译时优先理清案件进展、立场对立和行业走向。

sentences.en: In 2010, a federal judge shook America's biotech industry to its core.
sentences.zhReference: 2010 年，一名联邦法官的裁决撼动了美国生物技术产业的根基。

vocabulary.meaning: 从根本上震动、撼动根基。

sentences.en: Companies had won patents for isolated DNA for decades—by 2005 some 20% of human genes were patented.
sentences.zhReference: 数十年来，各家公司一直在为分离出来的 DNA 申请并获得专利——到 2005 年，人类基因中大约有 20% 已被授予专利。

vocabulary.meaning: 专利；作动词时指“申请并获得专利”。

sentences.en: But in March 2010 a judge ruled that genes were unpatentable.
sentences.zhReference: 但在 2010 年 3 月，一名法官裁定：基因不能被授予专利。

sentences.en: Executives were violently agitated.
sentences.zhReference: 企业高管们顿时情绪激动、反应强烈。

vocabulary.meaning: 焦躁不安的、情绪激动的。

sentences.en: The Biotechnology Industry Organisation (BIO), a trade group, assured members that this was just a "preliminary step" in a longer battle.
sentences.zhReference: 生物技术行业组织 BIO 作为一个行业协会，安抚其成员称，这不过是一场漫长战斗中的“初步步骤”。

sentences.en: On July 29th they were relieved, at least temporarily.
sentences.zhReference: 到了 7 月 29 日，他们至少暂时松了一口气。

sentences.en: A federal appeals court overturned the prior decision, ruling that Myriad Genetics could indeed hold patents to two genes that help forecast a woman's risk of breast cancer.
sentences.zhReference: 联邦上诉法院推翻了此前的裁决，认定 Myriad Genetics 的确可以持有两种与预测女性乳腺癌风险有关的基因专利。

sentences.en: The chief executive of Myriad, a company in Utah, said the ruling was a blessing to firms and patients alike.
sentences.zhReference: 位于犹他州的 Myriad 公司首席执行官表示，这一裁决对企业和患者来说都是一件好事。

sentences.en: But as companies continue their attempts at personalised medicine, the courts will remain rather busy.
sentences.zhReference: 但是，随着企业继续推进个性化医疗的探索，法院恐怕还会持续忙碌下去。

sentences.en: The Myriad case itself is probably not over.
sentences.zhReference: Myriad 这一案件本身很可能也还没有结束。

sentences.en: Critics make three main arguments against gene patents: a gene is a product of nature, so it may not be patented; gene patents suppress innovation rather than reward it; and patents' monopolies restrict access to genetic tests such as Myriad's.
sentences.zhReference: 反对基因专利的人主要提出三点理由：基因属于自然产物，因此不应被授予专利；基因专利压制创新而非奖励创新；专利垄断还会限制人们获得像 Myriad 那样的基因检测服务。
sentences.note: make arguments against 可译为“提出反对理由”或“提出反对论点”。

sentences.en: A growing number seem to agree.
sentences.zhReference: 越来越多的人似乎认同这一看法。

sentences.en: Last year a federal task-force urged reform for patents related to genetic tests.
sentences.zhReference: 去年，一个联邦特别工作组敦促对与基因检测相关的专利制度进行改革。

sentences.en: In October the Department of Justice filed a brief in the Myriad case, arguing that an isolated DNA molecule "is no less a product of nature...than are cotton fibres that have been separated from cotton seeds."
sentences.zhReference: 10 月，美国司法部就 Myriad 案提交了一份法律意见书，指出：分离出的 DNA 分子“并不比从棉籽中分离出的棉纤维更少属于自然产物”。

vocabulary.meaning: 分离出来的 DNA 分子。

sentences.en: Despite the appeals court's decision, big questions remain unanswered.
sentences.zhReference: 尽管上诉法院已经作出裁决，许多重大问题依然没有答案。

sentences.en: For example, it is unclear whether the sequencing of a whole genome violates the patents of individual genes within it.
sentences.zhReference: 例如，对整个基因组进行测序，是否会侵犯其中各个单独基因的专利，目前仍不明确。

sentences.en: The case may yet reach the Supreme Court.
sentences.zhReference: 这一案件最终甚至可能会提交到美国最高法院。

sentences.en: As the industry advances, however, other suits may have an even greater impact.
sentences.zhReference: 然而，随着行业继续发展，其他相关诉讼可能会产生更大的影响。

sentences.en: Companies are unlikely to file many more patents for human DNA molecules—most are already patented or in the public domain.
sentences.zhReference: 企业今后不太可能再为更多人类 DNA 分子申请专利——因为其中大多数不是已经申请了专利，就是已经进入公有领域。

sentences.en: Firms are now studying how genes interact, looking for correlations that might be used to determine the causes of disease or predict a drug's efficacy.
sentences.zhReference: 如今，各家公司正转而研究基因之间如何相互作用，寻找那些可用于判断疾病成因或预测药物疗效的相关性。

sentences.en: Companies are eager to win patents for "connecting the dots," explains Hans Sauer, a lawyer for the BIO.
sentences.zhReference: BIO 的律师汉斯·绍尔解释说，企业正急于为这种“把各个点连起来”的成果申请专利。

vocabulary.meaning: 把分散的信息联系起来。

sentences.en: Their success may be determined by a suit related to this issue, brought by the Mayo Clinic, which the Supreme Court will hear in its next term.
sentences.zhReference: 而它们能否成功，可能将取决于另一宗与此相关、由梅奥诊所提起并将在下一个审期由最高法院审理的案件。

vocabulary.meaning: 这里指“法院审期”，不是“学期/术语”。

sentences.en: The BIO recently held a convention which included sessions to coach lawyers on the shifting landscape for patents.
sentences.zhReference: BIO 最近举行了一次大会，其中还专门安排了若干场次，为律师讲解不断变化的专利形势。

vocabulary.meaning: 大会、年会；这里不是“传统习俗”。

sentences.en: Each meeting was packed.
sentences.zhReference: 每一场会议都座无虚席。
